title: Search, the core algorithm
summary: Trace a search for a key and say whether it is found.

hook.goal: Trace a search in a BST, listing the nodes visited, and say whether the key is found.

scenario.title: A guessing game
scenario.text: I am thinking of a number from 1 to 100. After each guess I only say "higher" or "lower".
scenario.reveal: Guessing 50 first is smartest: whatever I answer, half of the numbers are ruled out with one guess.

warmUp.question: In binary search on a sorted array, what does one comparison let you do?

options.reply: That is a linear search. Binary search does better with each comparison.

options.text: Discard half of the remaining values
options.reply: Yes. One comparison rules out half of what is left. A BST search works the same way.
Binary search needs an array that is already sorted; it does not sort it.

options.text: Jump straight to the largest value
options.reply: Binary search starts in the middle, not at the largest value.

explore.prompt: What did you do at each node?

options.text: Compared 60 with the node, then went left if 60 was smaller and right if it was larger
options.reply: Exactly. That one comparison per node is the whole search algorithm.

options.text: Checked the nodes from left to right
options.reply: That would visit nearly every node. Your path skipped most of the tree. What decided each turn?

options.text: Always went to the larger child
options.reply: That happened to work for 60 at 50, but not at 70. What decided each turn?

pages.title: How search works
steps: Compare the key you want with the node's key.
Empty spot: the key is not in the tree.
Each step throws away a whole subtree, so you visit at most height + 1 nodes. In tree T that is 3.

items.prompt: Click the nodes visited when searching for {20}, in order. Then give the result.

hints.text: At each node, ask: is {20} smaller or larger than this node?
The half of the tree that cannot hold {20} is now dimmed.

items.misconception: Thinking a search checks every node.

items.prompt: Searching for {65} in this tree: which nodes are visited, and what is the result?

options: {path}, then an empty spot: not found
{50}, {70}, {80}, then an empty spot: not found
{50}, {30}, {40}, then an empty spot: not found

hints.text: Is {65} smaller or larger than {50}? Then than {70}?
The half that cannot hold {65} is dimmed.

items.explanation: The search visits {path}, then reaches the empty {side} side of {endAt}: not found.
items.misconception: Stopping at a leaf instead of at an empty spot.

items.prompt: Searching for {45}: which node's empty side ends the search?

hints.text: Is {45} smaller or larger than {50}? Keep comparing until the spot you need is empty.
The half that cannot hold {45} is dimmed.

items.explanation: {path}, then the {side} side of {endAt} is empty, so the search stops there.
items.misconception: Stopping at a leaf instead of at an empty spot.

items.prompt: What is the most nodes a search can visit in this tree?

hints.text: Each comparison moves you one level down. How many levels are there?
The longest root-to-leaf path is highlighted.

items.explanation: At most height + 1 = {most} nodes, one per level.
items.misconception: Thinking a search checks every node.

items.prompt: What does a search return when it reaches an empty spot?

hints.text: If the key were in the tree, where would it have to be?
An empty spot is shown on the tree. Could the key be anywhere else?

items.explanation: Not found. If the key were in the tree, it would have to be in that empty spot.
items.misconception: Stopping at a leaf instead of at an empty spot.
